data: What questions do you have for the Government on the draft PWS? Please identify the specific section(s) if applicable.
Clarify workload, review boundaries, tools, and independence before asking firms to commit to delivery.
Please provide one relevant example of your company performing FedRAMP package review or comparable cloud security engineering work.
The examples span PMO review, independent assessment, provider implementation, and agency authorization work.

Please describe the labor mix needed to support FedRAMP 20x from end-to-end package reviews. Please identify which activities require senior engineering judgment and the qualifications or experience you would recommend for each role.
Senior judgment is widely emphasized; staffing ratios, automation roles, and delivery models vary.
Before beginning a review, how would you identify organizational conflicts of interest involving your company, affiliates, employees, or subcontractors?
Most describe pre-assignment screening; exclusion rules, lookback periods, and mitigation confidence differ.

Please explain how your personnel would determine whether a provider has adequately demonstrated a Key Security Indicator (KSI). Please distinguish among a security assertion, a security measure, evidence of implementation, evidence of effectiveness, verification, validation, and independent verification and validation. Please provide one concise example demonstrating these distinctions.
Evidence chains recur, but scope coverage, independent assessment, and the meaning of a passing check need care.

Please describe how your personnel would review a FedRAMP 20x Security Decision Record for completeness, technical sufficiency, consistency, and traceability. Please identify the evidence reviewers would expect and the conditions that would result in a question, finding, escalation, or recommendation that the package is not ready to proceed.
Four review dimensions are shared; readiness gates and class-specific requirements are less uniform.
How quickly could your team begin supporting active reviews, and how would you handle changes to FedRAMP rules, schemas, or procedures during performance?
Start-date claims use different clocks; access, calibration, and change control determine comparability.

Is there sufficient expert staffing available in the Washington DC metro area to support on-site requirements with the FedRAMP team at GSA, or is remote staffing outside the DC metro area necessary to maintain the highest quality of contractor staff?
Hybrid staffing is common, but remote work ranges from optional reach-back to a necessary delivery model.

The submissions describe several different vantage points on security evidence. Noblis claims long-running PMO support; FITS and Excentium describe assessor work; TES and Longevity cite 20x implementation experience; many others describe agency-side RMF, authorization, or cloud engineering. These are different forms of experience, not interchangeable proof of PMO review capability. Metrics and performance statements remain self-reported.

Describes building or operating cloud security, migration, or evidence automation.

Describes preparing or operating a provider’s FedRAMP package or offering.

Contains a drafting placeholder or answers a different question.

Example: VA VISN 21 (Sierra Pacific Network). ACE was a sub to Ordr, Inc. ACE did all of the work. Done in December 2023.

ACE rolled out a device-visibility and asset-inventory tool. It covered 10,870+ devices at 12+ VA sites. The hard part was the approval. We took the system through VA Assessment and Authorization (A&A) to a two-year ATO.

A FedRAMP reviewer checks that same work, from the other side of the table. The package needed a clear boundary. It needed data flows and inherited controls. Each NIST SP 800-53 control needed proof that held up. Each assessor question needed an answer tied to a file.

Related prime work: FMCS Azure Network and Systems Administration, TO 93310024F0012, done 09/2025. We ran identity, MFA, logs, scans, and security audits in a federal Azure tenant. ACE also holds HHS ASTP AI BPA 75P00125A00001. It calls for a FedRAMP High AI toolset.
Cites VA device-visibility authorization work and federal Azure operations.
Emphasizes hands-on implementation and evidence used to obtain an ATO, rather than PMO-side review.

Armavel provided enterprise cloud security and governance support to the Department of Veterans Affairs under VA Cloud Security Support. As a subcontractor to Maveris, Armavel supported secure cloud adoption across SaaS, PaaS, hybrid, and multi-cloud environments. Our team operationalized VA, FedRAMP, RMF, TIC 3.0, and Zero Trust requirements by reviewing security documentation and control implementation, conducting System Security Plan (SSP) gap analyses, evaluating shared-responsibility and control-inheritance, and prioritizing risk-based remediation actions. We helped establish the VA Cloud Security PMO and supported creation of a FedRAMP Program Office, improving the authorization process for cloud service providers and VA systems. We also developed security baselines and supported continuous monitoring, vendor incident-response validation, and governance activities that enable informed authorization decisions and accelerated compliance. Our reviews identified an average of seven security control misconfigurations or implementation deficiencies annually across CSP- and customer-responsible controls, informing corrective action.
Cites VA cloud governance, shared responsibility review, and authorization-process support.
Emphasizes agency governance and finding misconfigurations across responsibility boundaries.

Maryland Benefits, Maryland Department of Information Technology (DoIT), Aug 2016–Dec 2025, $11.0M. For nine years Assurit led security assessment and authorization for this cloud human services platform, a state system that exchanges data with CMS, SSA, IRS, and HHS and must meet each agency's security requirements. Our team reviewed and assessed authorization packages for 40 major applications and 8 general support systems (SSPs, SARs, POA&Ms, scan results, and configuration evidence) against a high-water-mark baseline spanning NIST SP 800-53 Rev 4/5, IRS Pub 1075, CMS MARS-E, and HIPAA. We tested whether controls worked, not just whether they were documented, and enforced a hard gate: no system proceeded to ATO with open critical or high findings. We assessed the security impact of every change and verified POA&M remediation through closure. Assessment covered 7,500 virtual cloud instances through continuous scanning, CIS/STIG compliance checks, and annual cloud penetration tests. Results: >90% compliance across 7,500 cloud assets, sustained compliance with CMS, IRS, SSA, and HHS security requirements, and Authority-to-Connect to the Federal Data Services Hub.
Describes nine years of assessment and authorization for Maryland Benefits.
Uses a state system with federal security obligations as its comparable example.

Department of Commerce, National Technical Information Service (NTIS), Contract 1331L523P13420146, Cloud9 as prime, awarded 2023, $4.48M with options. Cloud9 prepared the complete FedRAMP authorization package for the NTIS Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS) cloud offering for submission to GSA, then analyzed the deficiencies identified in its assessment and drove remediation through the POA&M to closure. Cloud9 also builds and maintains the NTIS Assessment and Authorization packages (FIPS 199, SSP, SAR, ISA, contingency plan, PIA, POA&M, ISCM reports) against NIST SP 800-53, schedules and tracks assessments in CSAM, and authored 20+ RMF-aligned SOPs. This is the same work PWS 3.2, 3.4, 3.5 and 3.7 describe: testing whether evidence supports security claims, writing findings tied to specific evidence, tracking issues to disposition, and keeping review procedures current. FY2024 CPARS rated Cloud9 Exceptional in Quality, Management and Regulatory Compliance, with no missed deadlines and no instances of non-compliance.
Cites preparation of the NTIS FedRAMP package, deficiency remediation, and agency A&A support.
Combines provider-package preparation with remediation and recurring agency documentation.

Under the PBGC ISSPO contract, our 12-person team reviews authorization packages the way GSA needs FedRAMP 20x packages reviewed. We support 17 systems, including the PBGC.gov, FM Interact, and FedHR Navigator FedRAMP boundaries, and deliver 12+ ATOs and 17 RMF assessments each year. Packages routinely arrive with stale evidence, controls marked implemented with no proof, and POA&Ms that cannot be traced to a finding. We fix this by reviewing every SSP, SAR, and POA&M against NIST SP 800-53 criteria, writing each finding with the requirement, the evidence examined, the condition observed, and the action needed, and tracking every question and response to closure in Power BI dashboards refreshed daily. We confirm outcomes with monthly automated vulnerability scans and annual FISMA assessments, and we filed FedRAMP Significant Change Requests to the AO 30 days before implementation. We are now moving all 17 systems from Rev 4 to Rev 5 through gap assessments, SSP refresh, remediation, and third-party attestation under a Plan-Do-Check-Act model with root cause analysis and COR-approved corrective action plans. The AO receives evidence-based recommendations and keeps every decision.
Cites PBGC package review, annual ATOs, findings traceability, and Rev4-to-Rev5 work.
Emphasizes recurring package quality and evidence gaps at agency scale.

As a subcontractor on the USDA FSIS Assessment and Authorization (A&A) III Plus Cloud Security Engineering contract, CVP provides direct FedRAMP compliance and cloud security engineering support across 11 system boundaries in a FedRAMP Azure Government environment. CVP's Cloud Security Engineers implement and assess NIST 800-53 Rev. 5 controls for cloud-based systems leveraging Azure Kubernetes, RedHat OpenShift, Redis, Application Gateway, and Azure DevOps. Our team ensured FedRAMP compliance for the FSIS Azure Government boundary housing all FSIS mission-critical and high-value assets supporting both national and international food safety operations. CVP developed and maintained System Security Plans, Control Implementation Summaries, and risk assessment documentation, earning Exceptional CPAR ratings across all performance categories. During performance, CVP's FSIS CISO formally recognized our Cloud Security Engineer for designing and enforcing advanced security controls aligned with NIST 800-53 Rev. 5 and FedRAMP requirements, supporting the hardening of FSIS's cloud environment. This work represents comparable experience to FedRAMP package review support sought under this PWS.
Cites USDA FSIS Azure Government security engineering across 11 boundaries.
Focuses on implementing and assessing controls within an agency cloud environment.

CMIC supports federal ATO reviews that include evaluating FedRAMP packages from the agency/ISSO perspective. Under the Department of State Consular Systems and Technology (DoS CST) effort, CMIC reviewed the overall Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) FedRAMP package, identified areas of potential concern, and continues to provide input on required vendor finding reports. CMIC identified several potential security issues, many involving known CVEs. Our team worked with the Department of State and the cloud provider to review the issues, identify mitigation steps and track progress. We continued reviewing the vendor's findings and proposed fixes to help ensure the issues were addressed to the client's satisfaction. 

When vulnerabilities identified through OCI security scans could not be immediately patched, CMIC worked with the client and vendor to evaluate alternative options. These included restricting network access, tightening security configurations, limiting access to affected services, and implementing additional monitoring where applicable. CMIC also helped track unresolved findings, document compensating controls and residual risk, and coordinate follow-up with the vendor.
Describes State Department review of an Oracle cloud package, vulnerabilities, and compensating controls.
Provides a concrete agency-side example of following unresolved risks through mitigation.

We recommend a tiered team in which senior engineers own judgment calls and analysts own volume.
Senior judgment (Technical Lead, Senior Cloud Security Engineer): scoping review plans by pathway and risk; deciding whether evidence demonstrates a KSI outcome; reviewing architecture, boundaries, inheritance, cryptography and data flows; separating schema errors from substantive deficiencies; recommending escalation or "not ready." Qualifications: 10+ years in cloud security, 5+ in FedRAMP or agency A&A, deep NIST SP 800-53 and 20x KSI knowledge; CISSP or CCSP plus a cloud security specialty (AWS, Azure or GCP).
Package Reviewer / Cloud Security Engineer: end-to-end KSI and evidence review, questions and findings, retest of corrected submissions. 5+ years; Security+ or CASP+ plus a cloud certification.
Automation / Data Analyst: machine-readable validation, schema conformance, traceability checks, metrics. Python, JSON/YAML, OSCAL experience.

Task Lead / Program Analyst: intake, tracking, aging, status reporting, metrics.
Describes a tiered review team instead of a past-performance example.

CyberStorm Defense brings extensive, verifiable past performance executing complex federal cloud security engineering and authorization package evaluations, having supported over 70 authorization efforts under NIST SP 800-37, NIST SP 800-53, and FedRAMP frameworks. Under active federal subcontracts including the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and the Missile Defense Agency (MDA) SHIELD IDIQ, CSD deploys automated DevSecOps pipelines and continuous cloud security posture assessments across multi-tenant commercial and federal cloud infrastructures. For federal cloud modernization initiatives, our engineers evaluate Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC) security compliance, validate container and Kubernetes hardening, and author audit-ready Security Assessment Reports (SARs) and POA&Ms. Every review is executed through our active GSA HACS schedule (SIN 54151HACS) with zero conflict-of-interest tool resale margins, backed by mandatory dual-engineer senior sign-off.
Claims 70+ authorization efforts, federal subcontracts, DevSecOps, and dual-engineer sign-off.
Emphasizes engineering and authorization volume without a named PMO-review engagement.

As an IRS CPO subcontractor (09/2020-01/2026), CybertLabs performed cloud security engineering completing 130+ security control assessments annually across cloud and on-premises systems. For new cloud projects, we reviewed cloud service provider packages, collected FedRAMP package identifiers, and evaluated service and deployment models, boundaries, inherited controls, shared responsibility, IAM, encryption, and logging. We examined SSPs, POA&Ms and vulnerability scans, verified implementation through live demonstrations, and resolved evidence gaps with stakeholders. We also delivered QA-reviewed SARs documenting evidence, findings and risks for Government authorization decisions. 
Significant Strengths: Our Splunk/Qmulos-enabled automated workflows replaced manual processes and improved data accuracy; we delivered Security Risk Assessments within two weeks of receiving required documentation. Our cloud and hybrid architecture reviews identified integration risks before deployment, supporting secure modernization and safeguarding sensitive IRS data. This experience thus prepares us to help FedRAMP scale evidence-based reviews while preserving Government risk-acceptance authority.
Describes IRS control assessments, cloud-package review, live demonstrations, and automated reporting.
Emphasizes agency-side evidence validation and QA-reviewed assessment reports.

From 2020-25, Deloitte provided large‑scale FISMA security assessment and FedRAMP‑comparable package review support at the FDIC. Our Security and Privacy Control Assessment (SCA) Team conducted 760+ security and privacy control assessments, covering 23,000+ controls across cloud, hybrid, and on‑premises systems, totaling 132 new/re-authorizations, 116 legacy approval systems, 493 continuous monitoring assessments, and 27 impact analyses. As part of all cloud assessments, the SCA team reviewed incoming FedRAMP packages for completeness, accuracy, and compliance, including systems seeking FDIC sponsorship for FedRAMP. 

Deloitte also provided cloud security engineering and FedRAMP advisory support to the U.S. Census Bureau for the Administrative Data Research Facility (ADRF). We advised the cloud service provider, Census Bureau stakeholders, and the Office of Information Security on allocating and implementing FedRAMP security controls under the shared responsibility model. We also provided guidance on closing control gaps and remediating issues identified through the 3PAO assessment process, supporting the Census Bureau’s sponsorship of the ADRF for FedRAMP authorization.
Cites large-scale FDIC assessments and Census provider advisory support.
Spans agency review and provider advice, perspectives relevant to its separate OCI answer.

From 2017 to 2025, as prime contractor to the Department of State (contract 19AQMM18C0040), Devis operated and developed the Refugee Processing Center systems (WRAPS and START). Devis maintained the A&A package on behalf of the system owner, migrated the environment from commercial AWS to AWS GovCloud, obtained the Authority to Operate, and wrote the application security documentation the ATO required. Devis monitored the environment with AWS CloudWatch, CloudTrail and Splunk and operated the SOC. In Q2 and Q3 FY2025, PRM's systems scored 100 percent against FISMA CIO cybersecurity metrics on State's E-CISO dashboard. Devis also automated data reconciliation into the program's data lake: procedures compared records extracted from ServiceNow against the source, flagged discrepancies, and re-pulled missing data, a data-consistency skill that carries over to the cross-artifact checks in PWS 3.3. This is comparable cloud security engineering work, not FedRAMP PMO package review. For review depth, Devis anticipates teaming with a FedRAMP-experienced partner.
Describes State Department A&A, GovCloud migration, SOC operations, and reconciliation automation.
Explicitly calls this comparable engineering, and anticipates a FedRAMP-experienced teammate.

EY supports FedRAMP across our federal client work and has also been through it ourselves, leading our own FedRAMP Moderate authorization on our Azure Government-based enclave. In delivering the scope of multiple task order under DOT's Cyber Security Information & Programs Services BPA, EY was instrumental in producing the following outcomes: 
- Supported 50+ cloud systems, conducting 67 event-driven and 55 annual assessments per FISMA cycle
-Reviewed cloud control inheritance using FedRAMP Customer Responsibility Matrices; examined boundaries, access, encryption, vulnerabilities, and POA&Ms; and traced evidence to controls, findings, and sources
-Operationalized 158 common controls to reduce duplicative testing and improve inheritance transparency
- Created a more reliable Business Impact Analysis process that helped DOT to correct misalignment between mission linkage and business continuity objectives
- Built custom agent using DOT-approved SI tool to draft SAR narratives from assessor-provided artifacts, reducing preparation from about 20 hours to 2, with human review of every output
-Delivered traceable, decision-ready findings while preserving Government decision authority
Cites its own enclave authorization and DOT assessments, inheritance, and AI-assisted report drafting.
Distinguishes assessor-provided evidence from drafting assistance with human review.

Treasury's Workplace.gov Community Cloud (TCloud) shows how Excentium delivers evidence-based federal cloud security review at scale. From May 2022 to May 2026, Excentium served as prime and A2LA-accredited FedRAMP IAS (formerly 3PAO) for one Moderate and one High system across AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, and Oracle Cloud. We completed 12 consecutive assessment cycles with zero missed SAR deadlines and zero authorization gaps and carried the program through a full NIST SP 800-53 Rev4 to Rev5 transition, four significant changes, and an expansion from one cloud (for TCloud High) to four on schedule.

The work matches the draft PWS: technical analysis across complex boundaries, findings traced to evidence, issue resolution through closure, and reporting that held up to Government review as requirements changed. Excentium also served as FedRAMP IAS for one of 12 authorized FedRAMP 20x Low pilot systems, applying the same discipline to outcome-based KSI evidence. On VA Enterprise Cloud Fax, we integrated FedRAMP PMO and assessor feedback to carry a FedRAMP High package into PMO review.
Cites Treasury multi-cloud assessments, a 20x Low pilot assessment, and VA package support.
Combines repeated independent assessment cycles with stated 20x pilot experience.

FITS performed a FedRAMP 20x assessment for Persona as part of the 20x pilot and Class C assessment. Our team evaluated the cloud service’s assessment scope and security practices, including the provider’s approach to demonstrating applicable Key Security Indicators (KSIs).
Assessors reviewed the provider’s security assertions, measures, supporting evidence, and verification and validation activities. We conducted interviews, examined technical artifacts and automated validation outputs, and evaluated whether the evidence supported the provider’s reported security outcomes.
FITS documented assessment results, identified evidence gaps and security risks, and communicated findings to the Persona’s relevant stakeholders. The engagement resulted in Certification.
This work demonstrates FITS’s ability to evaluate cloud security decisions, assess the reliability of evidence and automation, and communicate technically supported conclusions for FedRAMP 20x reviews.
Describes a Persona 20x pilot/Class C assessment, artifacts, interviews, and findings.
Offers an assessor-side 20x example rather than an agency RMF analogy.
Different sides of the same evidence

Graham Technologies (GRAHAM) performs comparable federal security assessment and cloud engineering on active DHS USCIS G-CACS III through Cybernamic, a Graham-led JV. Across 40+ major systems and 150+ subsystems, GRAHAM assesses NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 controls and supports ongoing authorization. We developed Continuous Compliance Insights (CCI), which aggregates security data, maps results to 70 automated controls, and exposes control-level evidence. CCI reduced manual review by approximately 40 hours per assessment. Our broader process modernization increased annual assessments from 16 to 50 while reducing staffing from 36 to 18 FTEs, saving more than $2.3M annually; assessment duration fell from 120 to 45 days. These are USCIS results, not projected FedRAMP savings. For GSA, we propose deploying or adapting CCI subject to approval, or replicating its validation workflow on premises using approved infrastructure. Automated checks would focus engineers on exceptions, evidence sufficiency, and risk; GSA retains final decisions.
Describes USCIS assessment modernization and its Continuous Compliance Insights tool.
Explicitly limits reported savings to USCIS and makes adaptation for GSA subject to approval.
Proposed tools are not verified outcomes

Guidehouse performed comparable cloud security assessments as prime contractor for NIH’s Center for Information Technology Risk Management Framework and Cybersecurity Support Services (75N97021F00002). Across NIH CIT’s AWS, Azure, GCP, and Microsoft 365 environments, encompassing 10 reportable FISMA systems, 50+ child systems, and 8,000+ assets, Guidehouse independently evaluates technical evidence to validate security-control implementations, identifies and prioritizes risk, and validates remediation before findings are closed. This experience requires assessing differing cloud implementations based on whether the implemented capabilities achieve intended security outcomes, rather than prescribing a single technical approach. Guidehouse has further applied this experience in developing GUSS, which can automate collection and analysis of technical security signals and map machine-generated evidence to control requirements. Together, these capabilities support rapid, evidence-driven engineering reviews of automated cloud security controls.
Describes NIH multi-cloud assessments, remediation validation, and a security-signal tool.
Links outcome-based judgment to automation of evidence collection.

Since 2014 IBSS has performed agency-side assessment and authorization for the Department of Defense Education Activity (DoDEA), as prime through 2022 and as a subcontractor since. IBSS security assessors and ISSOs led DoDEA's migration from DIACAP to the NIST Risk Management Framework, maintained the enterprise's major application packages in eMASS, assessed controls against NIST SP 800-53A and DISA STIGs, developed and reviewed security plans, assessment reports, and POA&Ms, and validated corrective actions. IBSS engineers also built DoDEA's Microsoft Azure landing zone to the DoD SCCA model. For DoDEA's cloud adoption, IBSS staff designed a FedRAMP and DoD Cloud Computing SRG control baseline tailored to K-12 education and delivered security assessments of commercial cloud service offerings (Azure, GCP, and SaaS applications) on the agency's behalf, reviewing provider security plans and evidence and reporting findings for Government disposition. Separation of duties is built in: several individuals work each package, and an assessor never validates a package on which they served as ISSO or program manager. This is agency-side review, not provider advisory work.
International Business Sales And Services Corp (IBSS Corp)
Describes DoDEA authorization, cloud assessments, an Azure landing zone, and separation of duties.
Explicitly distinguishes agency-side review from provider advisory work.

Since 2021, LDR has delivered FedRAMP-aligned authorization and monthly continuous monitoring for cloud services, plus 800-53 Rev 5 pre-assessments on 35+ systems annually across multi-cloud (AWS/Azure/GCP) and hybrid environments at the National Cancer Institute (National Institutes of Health). LDR managed authorization and ConMon for NIDAP, a Palantir Foundry instance in AWS serving 500+ researchers, spearheaded the first agency-sponsored GSA FedRAMP authorization for Broadcom Clarity, and performs ConMon for Druva, Broad FireCloud, Gen3, Qualtrics, DNAnexus and Medidata Clinical Cloud, using Tenable Nessus and HCL AppScan/Micro Focus Fortify scanning. LDR developed a FAST ATO pathway that cut SSP size from 300+ pages to under 20 via a Security Controls Traceability Matrix, and a Low-Impact SaaS pathway that delivers risk acceptance packages to the NCI CISO/CIO. LDR continues this support on NCI’s new five-year ECSS task order (9/2026-9/2031), covering risk management, security architecture, continuous monitoring and SOC support.
Describes NIH/NCI cloud authorization, continuous monitoring, and streamlined ATO pathways.
Focuses on recurring cloud oversight and agency authorization process changes.

LCE provides RMF support to various DoW customers. One example is the Naval Surface Warfare Center, Philadelphia Division (Code 104), where we review security authorization packages and conducting security assessment and authorization activities for cloud hosted and on premises systems. LCE evaluates security controls, reviews authorization documentation, assesses inherited and system specific controls, and analyzes residual risk to support ATO decisions. LCE leverages existing federal authorization packages where applicable and performs independent assessments when sufficient authorization artifacts are not available. Other activities include validating compliance with federal security requirements, reviewing security plans and supporting documentation, assessing cloud service provider controls, and providing recommendations to system owners and authorizing officials. This work requires deep knowledge of the NIST RMF process, security control assessment methodologies, risk analysis, and authorization package review, making it directly comparable to enterprise cloud security engineering and cybersecurity authorization support efforts.
Describes Navy authorization-package review, inherited controls, risk assessment, and ATO support.
Presents agency RMF work as comparable experience without claiming direct 20x PMO performance.

Longevity Consulting achieved FedRAMP 20x Class B (Low) authorization for its Riskuity SaaS platform (FR2604835605) as an active FedRAMP 20x pilot participant. Our engineers implemented and documented all 46 Key Security Indicators (KSIs), evaluated cloud architecture and system boundaries, generated machine-readable security artifacts, established a Trust Center, coordinated independent assessments, and implemented continuous monitoring.
This experience required translating requirements into verifiable measures, assembling and validating technical evidence, and resolving assessment findings. It provides firsthand insight into the evidence quality, technical dependencies, and documentation gaps that affect package readiness.

FedRAMP Definitions establish a shared understanding for terms when the plain-language meaning is not precise enough to support consistent use across the rules.
